key_insight: Ba2La2MnTe2O12 shows unusually strong frustrated 2D magnetic order inside a 3D hexagonal perovskite, with 120° AFM alignment in-plane and disordered moments along the c-axis.
engineering_relevance: The result highlights how crystal dimensionality can control magnetic ground states, informing the design of low-dimensional quantum materials with tunable frustration and spin dynamics.
method: NMR to probe local magnetic behavior
Neutron scattering to resolve magnetic ordering
Zero-field μSR to detect internal fields and spin fluctuations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a magnetic transition at TN ≈ 4.4 K and consistent signatures of strong spin fluctuations, 120° in-plane antiferromagnetic order, and large internal field distributions.
watch_item: The exotic 2D magnetic behavior is demonstrated at very low temperature, so practical use would require careful consideration of cryogenic operation and material stability.
paper_title: Strongly frustrated 2D magnetism in a 3D hexagonal perovskite
